                                          PROJECT NO. 58481

    RULEMAKING TO IMPLEMENT                            § PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
    LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION                         §
    STANDARDS UNDER PURA §37.0561                      §            OF TEXAS

                        ADDITIONAL COMMENTS OF SERENA POWER
                            ON PROPOSED NEW 16 TAC §25.194

         COMES NOW Serena Power (Serena) and files these additional comments on proposed

new 16 Texas Administrative Code (TAC) §25.194, relating to Large Load Interconnection

Standards. This proposed new rule would set forth the standards and criteria interconnecting a

large load customer to the ERCOT transmission network in a manner supporting business

development in this state. The Commission has requested that comments be filed by April 17,

2026, and therefore these comments are timely filed.

     INTRODUCTION AND REQUEST FOR COMMISSION GUIDANCE TO ERCOT

         Serena has previously filed comments on proposed 16 TAC §25.194. In its comments filed

on March 19, 2026, 1 Serena requested that the Commission increase the refundability of the

financial security in the amount of $50,000/MW that a large load customer must post when it

executes an Interim Agreement. 2 In the Proposal for Publication, if a large load customer

withdraws all or a portion of its requested peak demand for any reason, including if ERCOT does

not award the customer adequate capacity to allow a proposed project to proceed, only 20% of this

financial security (after applying the financial security to any costs detailed in subsection (g)(2)),

would be refundable.           In its earlier comments, Serena expressed its support for the

recommendation by Google and Lancium their March 10, 2026, proposed redlines, 3 that a more



1
     PUC Interchange Item 126, Serena Power Comments (March 19, 2026).
2
     Proposed §25.194(d)(10) and subsection (g).
3
     PUC Interchange Item 115, Google LLC and Lancium LLC, Joint Redlines for the Proposal for Publication at 2-
     3 (March 10, 2026) (Google/Lancium Redlines).
 reasonable approach would be one in which a maximum of $6.5 million of the financial security

would be non-refundable following a preliminary steady state study. As an alternative, if there is

not an initial steady state study as Google and Lancium recommended, rather than only 20% of

the posted financial security being refundable if a large load does not proceed to execute an

interconnection agreement following the Batch Study, Serena recommended that only 20% of the

posted financial security be non-refundable, since withdrawing or reducing the MW requested

before execution of an Interconnection Agreement (IA) would reduce, rather than increase, the

need for additional transmission commitments.         Either of these options would ensure that

significant financial security is posted at the outset but mitigate the expense that a large load must

bear if they determine that inadequate capacity is available for the commercial viability of the

proposed project.

       Serena continues to support this recommended change and respectfully requests that the

Commission provide guidance to ERCOT that this change should be incorporated into proposed

Planning Guide Revision Request (PGRR) 145, Batch Zero Process for Large Load

Interconnections, as part of its development of the Large Load Batch Study process. Since Serena

filed its original comments, the need to adopt Serena’s recommendations has increased since

ERCOT has indicated that it no longer will assume that a large load customer will be awarded the

full amount of its requested interconnection capability in Year 5 of the Batch Study, but that the

full award may be delayed for an additional undetermined number of years. This increased delay

in when a large load customer may have access to the full amount of its requested interconnection

capability likely will diminish the value of the unavailable capacity and could lead to a need to

withdraw the request for that capacity. Financial security related to the amount of unawarded

capacity after Year 5 of the Batch Study should be fully refundable.



                                                                     Serena Power Comments - Page 2
             COMMENTS ON SPECIFIC SECTIONS OF THE PROPOSED RULE

(f)     Interconnection Agreement.

        Serena respectfully recommends that the Commission delete subsection (f)(10) in its

entirety.   Subsection (f)(7) already requires a large load customer to pay a non-refundable

interconnection fee in the amount of $50,000 per MW of contracted peak demand when the

customer signs the interconnection agreement.          This fee is proposed to be paid to the

interconnecting TSP and applied to reduce the TSP’s rate base so as to reduce the impact of new

transmission construction on all ratepayers. Subsection (f)(8) also requires a large load customer

to post financial security for significant equipment and services needed to interconnect the large

load customer. In addition, subsection (f)(9) requires a large load customer to pay in cash all direct

interconnection costs through Contribution in Aid of Construction (CIAC). Serena appreciates

that the overarching goal of these requirements is to avoid residential customers from bearing the

cost of interconnecting large load customers to the ERCOT grid. Serena does not object to that

goal and supports requiring large load customers to be responsible for those costs that are directly

attributable to them, based on principles of cost causation.

        However, Serena recommends that subsection (f)(10) be deleted in its entirety since it

would require a large load customer to post financial security “for system upgrades that are

necessary to reliably serve the large load customer”. This obligation is overly vague because it is

not clear what upgrades will be solely attributable to a large load customer, or, if two or more large

load customers will need a particular system upgrade to reliably serve all of the large load

customers, how the financial security obligation would be apportioned. In addition, it is likely that

these upgrades also will benefit other customers that are not large loads. This adds yet more

complexity to the appropriate attribution of financial responsibility.       The apportionment of



                                                                     Serena Power Comments - Page 3
 financial responsibility for system upgrades will not be precise, has a significant potential to be

discriminatory, and could lead to the withdrawal of otherwise beneficial projects.

       In addition, making a specific large load customer fund remote transmission upgrades has

the potential to balkanize the ERCOT bulk transmission system, fundamentally altering the

funding mechanism of the “postage stamp” transmission cost allocation policy, which arguably

has been the most important policy of the past three decades for promoting unimpeded

development of the ERCOT competitive wholesale market.              Serena is very concerned that

changing this transmission cost allocation policy would be highly disruptive and have unintended

consequences. If transmission costs are paid by specific customers, then those customers would

naturally expect to have either exclusive rights or at least priority for use of that portion of the

system. This outcome would be wholly inconsistent with existing foundational policies in ERCOT

and should be avoided. Rather than adopting this requirement, Serena respectfully submits that an

improved approach to recovering transmission costs as is being developed in Project No. 58484,

Evaluation of Transmission Cost Recovery, is more appropriate to ensuring that large loads pay

their fair share of transmission system investments necessary to improve the ERCOT grid so that

it can reliably serve all the increased load that is coming to the state. In addition, this will allow

the continued use of the postage stamp transmission cost methodology that has served ERCOT

well and avoided protracted disputes regarding cost allocation that has plagued other electric

markets in the United States and delayed both generation and load interconnection. The costs that

are paid as a result of subsections (f)(7), (f)(8), and (f)(9) coupled with an improved transmission

cost recovery rule will be a better solution than proposed in subsection (f)(10). For these reasons,

Serena recommends that the Commission delete paragraph (10) in its entirety.




                                                                     Serena Power Comments - Page 4
 (g)    Withdrawal of all or a portion of requested peak demand or contracted peak demand.

       As discussed at the outset of these comments, Serena recommends that at least 80% of the

financial security posted by a large load customer, after payment of any amounts outstanding as

provided in subsection (g)(2), should be refundable. In addition, all financial security attributable

to peak demand that ERCOT does not forecast that it can serve after 5 years after the relevant

Batch Study and that the customer therefore withdraws from its original request should be fully

refundable.

       Serena recommends that subsections (g)(3) and (4) should be modified as follows:

       (3)     After applying the large load customer’s financial security to any outstanding

               amounts owed, the interconnecting DSP or the interconnecting TSP must refund

               80%20% of the balance to the large load customer within 60 days. Financial

               security posted for requested peak demand that the large load customer withdraws

               after ERCOT determines the demand cannot be served 5 years after the Batch Study

               must be refunded at 100%.

       (4)     After applying the financial security to any outstanding amounts owed and

               refunding 80%20% of the balance, the remaining 20%80% of the balance must be

               paid to the interconnecting TSP and applied by that TSP as an offset to the

               interconnecting TSP’s rate base in the earlier of the interconnecting TSP’s next

               interim rate proceeding or comprehensive rate proceeding.

(h)    Non-utilized capacity.

       Subsection (h) requires an interconnecting DSP or interconnecting TSP to identify a large

load customer’s non-utilized capacity if the large load customer fails, by 6 months, to satisfy a

milestone in its schedule for phased energization. There are many factors that are outside the



                                                                    Serena Power Comments - Page 5
 control of a large load customer that may cause a delay in meeting a portion of the customer’s

schedule for phased energization, including, for example, supply chain limitations, failure of long

lead time equipment, and other elements of force majeure.            Serena recommends that the

Commission increase the period over which a large load customer may fail to satisfy any portion

of its phased energization from 6 months to 12 months and also provide a large load customer with

the opportunity to demonstrate good cause if a further delay is necessary.

       In addition, consistent with the recommended changes to subsection (g) above, the

refundability provisions of subsection (h) should be increased to 80%.

       Serena recommends that subsection (h) should be revised as follows:

       (1)     Not later than 30 days after a large load customer fails, by 1246 months, to satisfy

               a milestone in its schedule for phased energization, the interconnecting DSP or the

               interconnecting TSP must notify ERCOT of the large load customer’s non-utilized

               capacity.

       (2)     Unless the large load customer demonstrates good cause to extend the delay beyond

               12 months, Wwithin 60 days of providing notice to ERCOT under this subsection,

               the interconnecting DSP or the interconnecting TSP must draw down on the large

               load customer’s financial security and apply the financial security to any

               outstanding amounts owed. Outstanding amounts owed include the following:

                   (A)     costs incurred by the interconnecting DSP or the interconnecting TSP to

                           fulfill the large load customer’s request for interconnection;

                   (B)     costs for equipment that the interconnecting DSP or the interconnecting

                           TSP procured and that cannot be canceled with a full refund;




                                                                    Serena Power Comments - Page 6
                      (C)     costs for construction that the interconnecting DSP or the

                             interconnecting TSP started and that cannot be canceled with a full

                             refund; and

                     (D)     costs for services that the interconnecting DSP or the interconnecting

                             TSP initiated and that cannot be canceled with a full refund.

          (3)    Unless the large load customer demonstrates good cause to extend the delay beyond

                 12 months, Wwithin 60 days of providing notice to ERCOT under this subsection

                 and after applying the large load customer’s financial security to any outstanding

                 amounts owed, the interconnecting DSP or the interconnecting TSP must refund

                 80%20% of the balance to the large load customer.

          (4)    After applying the financial security to any outstanding amounts owed and

                 refunding 80%20% of the balance, the remaining 20%80% of the balance must be

                 paid to the interconnecting TSP and applied by that TSP as an offset to the

                 interconnecting TSP’s rate base in the earlier of the interconnecting TSP’s next

                 interim rate proceeding or comprehensive rate proceeding.

                                           CONCLUSION

          Serena appreciates the opportunity to file these comments and appreciates the efforts of the

Commission Staff, ERCOT, and interested stakeholders to develop new regulations and processes

that will support the development and interconnection of large load customers in the ERCOT

region.
